title: Eggplant Involtini with White Bean Ricotta
cScaleSummary: C0 because the recipe contains no cholesterol-contributing animal-derived ingredients. The eggplant, cannellini beans, tomatoes, herbs, garlic, olive oil, miso, mustard, lemon, and seasonings contribute 0 mg cholesterol.
ldlActiveSummary: LDL-Active because the recipe is centered on beans, eggplant, tomato, herbs, garlic, lemon, and controlled unsaturated oil, with flavor built through roasting, simmering, and baking rather than saturated fat or cholesterol-containing ingredients.
intro: Involtini are Italian rolled preparations, often built from thin slices of eggplant, zucchini, meat, or fish wrapped around a savory filling. Eggplant versions are common in southern Italian cooking, where tomato, garlic, herbs, and olive oil do most of the heavy lifting. This version keeps the rolled, baked comfort of the dish while using white beans for body instead of cheese.
miseEnPlace: Prepare {{ingredient:eggplant}} as specified: sliced lengthwise 1/4 inch thick.

stepGroups.title: Roast the Eggplant
items: Brush the eggplants ({{quantity:eggplant}}) with the olive oil ({{quantity:olive-oil-eggplant}}) and season with kosher salt ({{quantity:salt-eggplant}}) and black pepper ({{quantity:black-pepper-eggplant}}). Arrange on parchment-lined sheet pans.
Roast for 18 to 22 minutes, until the slices are flexible, lightly browned, and dry enough to roll without tearing. Let cool slightly.

stepGroups.title: Make the White Bean Ricotta
items: Mash the cooked cannellini beans ({{quantity:cannellini-beans}}) with the olive oil ({{quantity:olive-oil-filling}}), lemon juice ({{quantity:lemon-juice-filling}}), lemon zest ({{quantity:lemon-zest}}), white miso ({{quantity:white-miso}}), Dijon mustard ({{quantity:dijon-mustard}}), garlic ({{quantity:garlic-filling}}), kosher salt ({{quantity:salt-filling}}), and black pepper ({{quantity:black-pepper-filling}}) until creamy but still slightly textured.
Stir in the fresh basil ({{quantity:basil-filling}}) and fresh parsley ({{quantity:parsley-filling}}). The filling should be thick enough to hold its shape when spooned.

stepGroups.title: Make the Tomato Sauce
items: Heat the olive oil ({{quantity:olive-oil-sauce}}) in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic ({{quantity:garlic-sauce}}) and red pepper flakes ({{quantity:red-pepper-flakes}}). Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add the crushed tomatoes ({{quantity:crushed-tomatoes}}), kosher salt ({{quantity:salt-sauce}}), and fresh oregano ({{quantity:oregano}}). Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until slightly thickened.

stepGroups.title: Roll and Assemble
items: Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce in a baking dish.
Place a spoonful of white bean ricotta at one end of each roasted eggplant slice. Roll up and place seam-side down in the baking dish.
Spoon the remaining tomato sauce over the rolls.

stepGroups.title: Bake and Rest
items: Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the sauce is bubbling and the rolls are heated through.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving so the filling firms slightly and the rolls hold together.

stepGroups.title: Serve
items: Finish with the fresh basil ({{quantity:basil-finish}}) and fresh parsley ({{quantity:parsley-finish}}). Serve warm.
